note: Longevity medicine. Practical, evidence-based, occasionally tedious.

t: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde

note: The foundational liberal argument. Still the clearest defense of free thought.
The first existentialist novel. The narrator's voice will get under your skin.
The novel that started Romanticism and inspired copycat suicides. Brief, intense.

note: The original meditation on creation, hubris, and what we owe what we make. Holds up.

Yalom's letter to new therapists. Wise, humane, full of clinical insight even for non-therapists.
